column1: Project Meeting Procedure:

First fifteen minutes of scheduled project meeting: Project Group fills out "Tasks completed before the PM" and "Time spent on completed tasks" for each student (updating the group on individual progress)

After the first fifteen minutes, the tutor will join the meeting sometime during the scheduled project meeting and discuss with students what they have done individually also in alignment with the issueboard
Please note: Be ready to discuss with the tutor as soon as they come into the room. One group member projects the file on the screen. EVERYONE joins the discussion.
Tutor together with the students flags the two rows"Tasks completed before the PM" and "Time spent on completed tasks" per student according to:

column3: Students accomplished their tasks; good contribution

Students did not accomplish assigned task but have a valid reason (here, only technical reasons apply e.g. library connection not as easy as thought, unexpected programming issues, ...); Reasons become clear in the reflection part.
Students were lacking effort to accomplish tasks. Reasons become clear in the reflection part.

column1: If needed, tutor adds comments e.g. if needed time sounds too long, or tutor has doubts about honesty, or student is absent)
Tutor discusses open questions/project management/etc.
Tutor leaves
Group continues working on their tasks until the end of the scheduled project meeting.

Last fifteen to thirty minutes of scheduled project meeting: Group fills out the "Tasks to be completed before next PM" and the "Estimated time" at the end of the scheduled project meeting. Students with a yellow/red flag reflect on their flag by:

column2: 1) Description: Provide a clear, factual account of the situation without analysis or judgment. Example: Our team had to train and evaluate a neural network on a text dataset. I was assigned hyperparameter tuning but submitted incomplete code, causing delay
2) Analysis: Why did it happen? Example:  I lacked confidence in the library to use and avoided working on it until it was too late
3) Action:  Outline specific steps you will take to improve in the future. Example: I'll test code in smaller chunks and commit regularly so teammates can help if needed.
